headline: Schwarber's slam caps six-run 6th in 11-7 win
recap: The Phillies beat the Astros 11-7 on Wednesday night at Citizens Bank Park, scoring six runs in the sixth inning to turn a one-run deficit into a rout. Houston took a 4-0 lead in the top of the third: Yordan Alvarez's double scored Cam Smith, Isaac Paredes followed with a two-run homer, and Yainer Diaz's single drove in Jose Altuve. Philadelphia answered in the bottom of the inning, tying it 4-4 on RBI singles from Trea Turner, Bryce Harper and Luis Arraez -- Harper's hit also scored Turner and came with a throwing error that put Harper on second. Cam Smith's two-run homer put Houston back ahead 6-4 in the fourth, and Turner's solo home run in the fifth cut it to 6-5. The Phillies broke it open in the sixth: Edmundo Sosa's RBI single tied it 6-6, a bases-loaded walk to Bryan De La Cruz put them ahead 7-6, and Kyle Schwarber followed with a grand slam -- his 44th home run of the season -- for an 11-6 lead. Houston scored once more in the seventh on a Paredes RBI single but got no closer. Cristopher Sánchez worked six innings, allowing six runs, to improve to 17-5; Bryan King took the loss after entering in the sixth and retiring no one before the Phillies pulled away.
The win keeps the Phillies at 82-64, alone in second place in the NL East, three games behind the division-leading Braves (85-61), and riding a one-game winning streak.

Philadelphia closes out the series with Houston Thursday afternoon at Citizens Bank Park, with first pitch at 1:05 PM ET. Zack Wheeler starts for the Phillies opposite Astros right-hander Cristian Javier. DraftKings has the Phillies favored at -196 on the moneyline, with Philadelphia -1.5 on the run line (+110).
